decisive_items: pancytopenia: platelet count 85×10^9/L, white-cell count 2.3×10^9/L (neutrophils 1.3×10^9/L, monocytes 0.2×10^9/L), and hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL
Skin biopsy showed dermal neutrophils with upper dermal edema and a subepidermal blister, consistent with bullous Sweet’s syndrome
Her blood counts remained low: hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, white-cell count 1.7×10^9/L (neutrophils 0.5×10^9/L, monocytes 0.1×10^9/L), and platelets 49×10^9/L
response.rationale: Aplastic anemia best explains persistent pancytopenia refractory to ITP therapy, with Sweet syndrome as an associated immune-mediated manifestation. ITP cannot account for leukopenia/anemia, SLE is excluded by negative ANA, and Sweet syndrome alone does not explain the underlying bone marrow failure.

rejected.why: Pancytopenia is a laboratory finding, not an etiologic diagnosis.
ITP explains only thrombocytopenia and is contradicted by leukopenia/anemia and lack of response to steroids and IVIG.
ANA was negative and there were no clinical features of lupus; only a family history was present.
Bullous Sweet's syndrome is confirmed by biopsy but does not explain the persistent pancytopenia and is best viewed as associated with an underlying hematologic disorder.
